title: Reading Drill — Checking a new market awning — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Checking a new market awning — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The market buildings team had been asked to investigate water dripping at one end onto a busy walkway in Ravensmere. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the area wetted during showers, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a eight-week comparison, the team used chalk outlines at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because wind during rain might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a slight change in the angle. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
